entries.title: Proverbs 11:1
segments: Dishonest practices in trade are so prevalent, that multitudes have but a feeble apprehension of their great wickedness.  But God regards them all with abhorrence; and unless repented of and forsaken, they will bring upon men his righteous indignation in this world, and will exclude them from heaven.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:2
segments: A haughty spirit is a sure precursor of an ignominious fall; but humility is the highway to permanent honor.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:3
segments: Integrity is a sure guide; it leads men by a safe path, and brings them out in a safe place.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:4
segments: In the day of wrath; of God's wrath.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:5
segments: Shall direct his way; shall make his way plain, so that he shall have no occasion of stumbling.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:8
segments: Cometh in his stead; cometh into trouble in his place.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:9
segments: All slanderers are hypocrites; under the pretence of rebuking their neighbor's faults, they are gratifying their own envy and malice.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:11
segments: Righteous men are the best defence of a city, and wicked men its most imminent peril.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:12
segments:
Despiseth his neighbor; not only feels contempt in his heart, but expresses it in his words and actions. 
 
True self-knowledge makes us forbearing in speaking of the faults of others.  The man who busies himself in publishing his neighbor's failings, thereby proclaims his own folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:14
segments: When God would destroy a nation, he takes away its wise counsellors, and gives it up to the control of wicked and weak men.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:16
segments: A gracious woman; literally, a woman of grace, that is, a winning and attractive woman.  Her attractiveness includes mental as well as bodily accomplishments.  She is a woman of discretion, for "a fair woman without discertion" does not retain her honor;

. 
 
  Retaineth; gains and keeps.  There is here a tacit comparison: As strong men gain riches, so a gracious woman gains honor.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:17
segments: The principal harvest of mercy and cruelty is reaped by those who exercise them.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:18
segments: A deceitful work; a work which deceives and disappoints his hopes.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:21
segments: Though hand join in hand; though every combination and effort to escape punishment be resorted to.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:22
segments:
In a swine's snout; that is, very much out of place. 
 
Beauty without discretion is a calamity instead of a blessing.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:23
segments:
Only good; in its issue.  His hopes of good are all realized. 
 
  Is wrath; ends in wrath.  Instead of the good for which he hoped, he receives wrath from God.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:24
segments:
Scattereth; distributes his wealth in deeds of kindness. 
 
True Christian liberality is the road to prosperity.  It secures God's blessing upon our gain, and makes it profitable to ourselves and to others.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:26
segments:
Withholdeth corn; hoards it up in time of famine, in order to sell it at a high price. 
 
The worst extortioner is he who takes advantage of a public calamity to fill his own coffers at the expense of the poor.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:27
segments:
Seeketh good; occupies himself in doing good. 
 
  Procureth favor; from God and man.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:29
segments:
Troubleth his own house; involves his family in misery by his misconduct. 
 
  The wind; emptiness and disappointment.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:30
segments: Fruit of the righteous; the results which he produces.

entries.title: Proverbs 11:31
segments: Recompensed; chastised for his sins.  The Greek version of the Seventy renders this verse thus: "If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?" which gives the same general sense, and is followed by,

. 
 
The severity with which God punishes his offending children, is a solemn warning to the wicked of the awful destruction which awaits them.
